title: Personal Hygiene & Self-Care
subtitle: Puberty changes the rules. Nobody usually explains why.
objectives: Explain why body odour appears at puberty
Describe correct handwashing and why it works
Explain how tooth decay happens and how brushing stops it
Describe basic skin, hair and nail care
Explain self-care as more than washing

cards.title: Sweat has no smell
cards.text: That is a real fact, not a comforting one. Fresh sweat is almost odourless. Bacteria on your skin do the rest.

cards.title: One switches on at puberty
cards.text: Eccrine glands cover most of your body and produce watery sweat. Apocrine glands are different, and they start working at puberty.
points: **Eccrine:** everywhere, watery, for cooling.
**Apocrine:** armpits and groin, thicker fluid.
**Bacteria feed on apocrine sweat.**
**The smell is the bacteria**, not you.

cards.title: This is why the routine has to change
cards.text: The washing that was enough at nine is not enough at twelve. The glands doing the work are different ones.
points: **Nothing went wrong.** A system switched on.
**Daily showering** becomes necessary, not optional.
**Clean clothes matter** as much as clean skin.
**Deodorant masks. Antiperspirant reduces.**

cards.title: Each one, and the reason behind it
cards.text: Tap through. Every item has a mechanism, not just a rule.

options: Bacteria feeding on sweat from apocrine glands
Sweat itself, which has a strong smell
question.explain: Fresh sweat is nearly odourless. Apocrine glands switch on at puberty and bacteria do the rest.

cards.title: Soap does something specific
cards.text: Soap molecules pull apart the fatty outer layer of many germs. They also lift the rest off so water carries it away.
points: **Twenty seconds** is the usual guidance.
**Backs of hands and between fingers** get missed.
**Under the nails** is the most missed spot.
**Rinsing alone** leaves most of it behind.

question.text: Rinsing your hands with water alone removes germs about as well as using soap.
question.explain: Soap breaks up the fatty outer layer of many germs and lifts the rest off. Water alone leaves most behind.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is teeth, skin and what self-care actually covers. Take a breath.

cards.title: A cavity is bacteria producing acid
cards.text: Bacteria in your mouth eat sugar and release acid. The acid dissolves enamel. That is the whole process.

cards.title: Plaque is the film they live in
cards.text: Plaque is a soft layer of bacteria. Left alone it hardens into tartar, which a brush can no longer remove.
points: **Brush twice a day**, two minutes each.
**Enamel does not grow back.**
**Snacking often** keeps the acid attack running.
**Flossing reaches** where the brush cannot.

cards.title: Enamel has no respawn
cards.text: Almost everything in your body repairs itself. Tooth enamel is one of the few things that genuinely does not.
points: **Bone heals. Skin heals. Enamel does not.**
**A filling is a patch**, not a repair.
**Damage here is permanent.**
**That is why the routine is non-negotiable.**

question.text: Why can't a toothbrush remove tartar?
options: Tartar is hardened plaque and needs a dentist to remove
Toothbrushes are too soft by law
Tartar only forms on the tongue
question.explain: Plaque is soft and brushable. Once it hardens into tartar, brushing no longer shifts it.

cards.title: Oil production rises at puberty too
cards.text: The same hormones that start apocrine sweat also increase skin oil, which is why acne is common at your age.
points: **Acne is not caused by being dirty.**
**Scrubbing harder makes it worse.**
**Cut nails straight across** to avoid ingrowth.
**Wash hair** as often as it gets oily.

cards.title: Gear is part of hygiene
cards.text: Wraps, gloves and kit hold sweat and bacteria. Damp gear in a closed bag is how skin infections spread in a gym.
points: **Dry wraps between sessions.**
**Air the gloves**, do not seal them in.
**Shower soon after training**, not hours later.
**Never share** wraps, towels or a mouthguard.

cards.title: Self-care includes rest and asking
cards.text: Washing is the visible part. Sleep, food, rest days and saying when something is wrong are the same job.
points: **Looking after yourself** is a skill, not vanity.
**Telling an adult early** is part of it.
**A routine removes the decision.**
**Same order, same time, every day.**

question.text: Acne is caused by not washing your face enough.
question.explain: It is driven by hormones raising oil production. Scrubbing harder irritates skin and makes it worse.

terms.def: Sweat gland found all over the body. Watery sweat, for cooling.
Sweat gland in the armpits and groin that switches on at puberty.
A soft film of bacteria on teeth. Brushing removes it.
Hardened plaque. Only a dentist can remove it.
The hard outer layer of a tooth. It does not grow back.
Masks or slows odour. Antiperspirant reduces the sweat itself.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Sweat is odourless.** Bacteria make the smell.
**Soap breaks germs apart.** Water alone does not.
**Enamel does not grow back.**
**Acne is hormones**, not dirt.

quiz.text: Which sweat glands start working at puberty?
quiz.explain: Apocrine glands sit in the armpits and groin and produce a thicker fluid bacteria feed on.
quiz.objective: Explain why body odour appears at puberty

quiz.text: Fresh sweat has a strong smell of its own.
quiz.explain: False. Fresh sweat is nearly odourless. The smell comes from bacteria feeding on it.
quiz.objective: Explain why body odour appears at puberty

quiz.text: What is the difference between deodorant and antiperspirant?
options: Deodorant masks odour; antiperspirant reduces sweating
They are two words for the same product
Deodorant kills all skin bacteria permanently
quiz.explain: One addresses the smell, the other addresses the sweat itself.
quiz.objective: Explain why body odour appears at puberty

quiz.text: How does soap help remove germs?
options: It breaks apart their fatty outer layer and lifts them off the skin
It changes the colour of germs
quiz.explain: That is why soap and twenty seconds beat a quick rinse every time.
quiz.objective: Describe correct handwashing and why it works

quiz.text: Which part of the hands is most often missed when washing?
quiz.explain: Under the nails, then between the fingers and the backs of the hands.
quiz.objective: Describe correct handwashing and why it works

options: Bacteria producing acid that dissolves enamel
quiz.explain: Bacteria eat sugar and release acid. The acid dissolves enamel, and enamel does not grow back.
quiz.objective: Explain how tooth decay happens and how brushing stops it

options: A soft film of bacteria on the teeth
The hard outer layer of a tooth
quiz.explain: Brushing removes plaque. Once it hardens into tartar, only a dentist can.
quiz.objective: Explain how tooth decay happens and how brushing stops it

quiz.text: Tooth enamel grows back once damage stops.
quiz.explain: False. Bone and skin heal; enamel does not. A filling is a patch, not a repair.
quiz.objective: Explain how tooth decay happens and how brushing stops it

quiz.text: Why does acne become common at puberty?
options: Hormones increase the skin's oil production
It is caused by eating chocolate
quiz.explain: The same hormones that start apocrine sweat raise skin oil. Scrubbing harder makes it worse.
quiz.objective: Describe basic skin, hair and nail care

quiz.text: How should nails be cut to avoid ingrowth?
quiz.explain: Cutting down into the corners is what lets a nail grow into the skin.
quiz.objective: Describe basic skin, hair and nail care

quiz.text: Why should training gear be dried between sessions?
options: Damp gear holds bacteria and spreads skin infections
Wet gear is against the rules
quiz.explain: Damp wraps sealed in a bag are how skin infections move around a gym.
quiz.objective: Explain self-care as more than washing

quiz.text: What else counts as self-care besides washing?
options: Sleep, food, rest and telling someone when something is wrong
quiz.explain: Washing is the visible part. The rest of it is the same job.
quiz.objective: Explain self-care as more than washing

teacher.summary: Week 10 closes the MAPEH Health strand with personal hygiene and self-care. It is written to be read by a boy going through puberty without embarrassment, by giving mechanisms instead of instructions: apocrine glands rather than 'you smell now', hormones rather than 'wash your face'. The two claims most worth him keeping are that fresh sweat is odourless and that acne is not caused by being dirty, because both replace shame with a cause. The gym-gear card is included because he trains, and damp wraps are the most likely route to a real skin infection at his age. Self-care is explicitly widened at the end to include rest and speaking up.
discussion: Ask him to explain in his own words why the routine had to change this year.
Ask what soap does that water alone cannot.
Ask which body tissues repair themselves and which do not.
Ask what part of self-care has nothing to do with washing.
teacher.extension: Have him write his own morning and evening routine as a short checklist, in order, with a one-line reason next to each item. If he cannot give a reason, the item comes off the list.
misconceptions: 'Sweat smells.' Fresh sweat is nearly odourless; bacteria feeding on it produce the smell.
'Acne means you are dirty.' It is hormonal, and scrubbing harder irritates the skin.
'A quick rinse is enough.' Soap breaks up the fatty coat of many germs; water alone does not.
'Damaged enamel will heal.' It does not regrow. That is why the brushing routine matters so much.
